ruling.recommended_action: Escalate to a Ryde human reviewer: (1) SAFE-1 review of the driver's 09:05 message "Shut up and let me drive" (F9) to the rider who had just questioned the route (F8) — pending that review do not execute the fare refund; (2) if cleared, process the route-deviation refund of $7.25 (5.14 km × $1.4102/km, F3/F4) as a Ryde voucher, and record the RD-1 breach against the driver. No account flag (RD-6 'repeated' not met, F17).
ruling.reasoning:
Route limb. The trip is a metered RydeTAXI job (F7), so any unexempted detour mileage passes straight into the fare. One off-route segment is recorded, 09:00–09:11, 6.89 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.75 km, +5.14 km and up to 1481 m off the optimal line (F3); the whole trip ran 21.4 km against 15.9 km optimal (F1). Under RD-1 each such segment stands unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it.

No excuse applies. RD-4 requires a `traffic-incident-*` fact on the replaced stretch reported before the detour; F14 records no incident near the route during the trip window, and the two speed-band records (F12 PIE band 5, 40–49 km/h; F13 KPE band 4, 30–39 km/h) are not incidents and not band 1/2, so RD-4(b) leaves them as corroboration only — they neither exempt the segment nor excuse it [F12][F13][F14][RD-4].

Consent also fails. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F10), and the only rider message is the 09:04 question "Why are we going this way?" (F8), sent after the segment began at 09:00; there is no rider message naming a road, stop or route, so nothing engages RD-3(a) or either branch of RD-5 [F8][F10][RD-3][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him (F11) is a claim in his own statement, which is not rider consent and is contradicted by the absence of any incident record [F11][F14][RD-5]. The segment therefore counts, on the stipulated ground consent_after_or_none [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

Amount if executed. RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at the trip's own rate from the fare record: $30.22 ÷ 21.43 km = $1.4102/km; 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The balance of the billed whole-trip excess ($7.83 for 5.55 km, F4) is not attributable to any segment and is expressly non-refundable under RD-2 [F4][RD-2]. The $0.11 meter waiting item (F5) is chargeable metered waiting time under RD-3(c) and no unpublished add-on appears in the F7 breakdown, so no FARE-1 refund arises [F5][F7][RD-3][FARE-1].

Why I do not rule on the money. SAFE-1 requires the judge to screen the chat, the complaint and the driver's statement. The rider's complaint says she "felt unsafe", and the driver's reply to her routing question was "Shut up and let me drive" (F9) — read in context, a hostile, abusive instruction aimed at the rider, not a mere route-argument remark, and both advocates read it the same way [F8][F9][F10][SAFE-1]. That makes the safety screen at least suspected, and SAFE-1 directs that such a case is not decided automatically but goes to a human with a factual summary. I therefore escalate rather than execute the otherwise correct $7.25 partial refund.

Account action. Neither party has an upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (rider 0, driver 0) [F16][F17], so RD-6's "repeated" condition is not met and no flag_account attaches [F17][RD-6] — the RD-1 breach is nonetheless recorded against the driver.

segment_findings.reason: Complete, fully timestamped chat record (F10) shows no rider message before the 09:00 segment start agreeing to any route; the only rider message is the 09:04 question 'Why are we going this way?' (F8), sent after the segment began, and the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him (F11) is his own claim, not rider consent (G11). No RD-3(a) named place and no RD-5 general or named-road agreement, so the segment's 5.14 extra km are unexempted under RD-1 and refundable under RD-2.

Accepted, and decisive: the driver's 09:05 message 'Shut up and let me drive' (F9), read with the rider's 09:04 question (F8) in the complete chat record (F10), is abusive language aimed at the rider under SAFE-1, so the case escalates rather than being decided on the fare facts.
Accepted: F16/F17 show no upheld route dispute in 90 days for either party, so RD-6's 'repeated' condition fails and no flag_account attaches [F17][RD-6].

Accepted: no qualifying traffic incident on the replaced stretch (F14) and the band records (F12 PIE band 5, F13 KPE band 4) are not band 1/2 and are corroboration only, so RD-4 cannot exempt the segment [F14][F12][F13][RD-4].

Accepted as context but rejected as an excuse: both bands were live during 09:00–09:11 (F12/F13/F3), yet RD-4(b) makes speed bands corroboration only and never a standalone exemption [F12][F13][RD-4].
Correct arithmetic but no award issueable while the case escalates under SAFE-1; the $0.58 remainder of the billed excess (F4) is indeed non-refundable under RD-2 [F3][F4][RD-2].
